correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 18–85 in time s=γt with h=γ₂/γ. The three faces of the symmetric physical triangle point inward or tangent. Z=u+3v/2 satisfies Z′=−v(u+2hv); on v=0 the vector field has v′=2u², so the origin is the only invariant subset where dissipation vanishes. Compactness and LaSalle give global clearance. For any nonzero initial state uniqueness gives Z>0 at finite times. The equation for q=v/Z has a forcing tending to zero and a coefficient tending to −2h, so q→0. The equation for v/Z² has forcing tending to 2 and coefficient tending to −2h, so v/Z²→1/h. Then (Z⁻²)′→2/h and sZ²→h/2. Returning to physical time gives the two amplitudes as stated, including t v→1/(2γ). The conclusion is on the symmetric triangle only; the zero orbit has no positive tail. Read the verification notes and checker as evidence descriptions, not as an independent execution or a proof; the limits are certified here by the analytic argument, not by a numerical run.
residual_risks: No claim about asymmetric initial data, off-critical parameters, or rates uniform in h.
